name: recreated-session-starts-fresh
description:
A person messages a conversation whose session was deleted. The second message must start a FRESH session that answers it, with none of the deleted session's conversation in its context.

A session's name is derived from (channel, key), and its memory scope is keyed by that name, not the CR's UID. The transcript outlives the CR on purpose: turns are append-only, signed audit evidence. So the second message used to mint a session under the SAME name, onto the deleted one's transcript. The runner read that as a resume: turn 0 already existed, so spec.prompt was never placed. A predecessor ending on the agent's reply parked without a word; one ending on a tool result — as this one does, on agent_work_complete's — ran the OLD conversation again. Either way the person's message was lost, and the deleted session's tool output — never re-authorized for whoever was asking now — became the new session's context. channelsd now mints the successor under the next free name instead (pipeline.freshSessionName).

What this pins, step by step. Step 4 is the second session's FIRST model call: userTextContains proves the new message was placed as its opening prompt rather than parked on, and requestNotContains proves nothing the first session read is in its context at all — not merely absent from the latest tool result. Step 5 asserts on the TOOL RESULT the second session's own call returned, not on the reply text, since a scripted reply says the same words either way. If the name is ever reused again, step 4 is answering the old conversation: its latest user text is the FIRST message and Acme Payroll is in its context, so both of its checks fail.
